newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian refinery runs fall to 43 pct of demand.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian refinery runs fall to 43 pct of demand.

text.p: Nigerian oil refineries are producing only 43 percent of the nation's gasoline requirement, causing a long-running fuel shortage in parts of the country, oil officials said on Thursday.

"The current shortage is because the refineries are not producing optimally," said a senior official of the Pipelines and Product Marketing Company (PPMC), a subsidiary of state oil firm, the Nigerian National Supply Corp (NNPC).
He was commenting on a report in the semi-official Daily Times that Nigeria's three functioning oil refineries were operating in fits.

"Supplies from the three functioning refineries in Kaduna, Warri and Port Harcourt had dropped to 7.74 million litres per day compared to the national consumption level of 18 million litres," the paper said.
NNPC has been largely silent on the fuel shortage that has gripped Africa's leading oil producer since last month and has intermittently eased only to resume after a few days respite.
In Lagos and some cities in the southwest, long queues for fuel at pump stations have become a regular feature for weeks.

Daily Times said output from the newer Port Harcourt refinery had halved while the old one was down. It said Kaduna in the north was producing 1.7 million litres of fuel daily instead of three million litres but was silent on Warri refinery.
Fuel shortage is common in Nigeria, where poor management has often reduced output of the four refineries which have a combined total capacity of 445,000 barrels per day.
NNPC officials said the current epileptic performance of the refineries was due to lack of funds to effect maintenance.
The government budgeted $200 million this year to overhaul the refineries but the officials said the money was yet to be released to NNPC.
